1	---
2	name: caveman
3	description: >
4	  Ultra-compressed communication mode that cuts output tokens while keeping
5	  technical accuracy. Levels: lite, full, ultra and the wenyan variants. Use for
6	  /caveman, "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "be brief" or "less tokens".
7	---
8	
9	Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.
10	
11	## Persistence
12	
13	Default style for this whole session, every response, until user say "stop caveman" or "normal mode". Keep terse on long sessions no filler drift.
14	
15	Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra|wenyan-lite|wenyan-full|wenyan-ultra|off`.
16	
17	## Rules
18	
19	Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.
20	
21	Never drop not/never/no/only/except flip meaning worse than any token saved. Numbers, units exact.
22	
23	Never ADD word to sound caveman. Compression only style never grow output. No inserted pronoun or copula to fake broken grammar: "when it not" cost one token more than "when not" and say same thing. Keep correct verb form when correct form cost same "sees" one token, "see" one token, so mangle buy nothing and read worse. Same rule as abbreviations and arrows: if caveman phrasing not shorter than plain phrasing, use plain.
24	
25	Clarity register: mix ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English into caveman, always. One idea per sentence. Sentence short, target 20 words max. Active voice. Present tense where true. One word one meaning: same term for same thing every time, no synonym rotation. Instruction = imperative: "Run X", not "X should be run". Noun cluster 3 words max. Pronoun only with one clear referent, else repeat noun. Caveman cut filler; STE keep what make meaning unambiguous. Conflict between them → clarity win.
26	
27	Tool calls: fire direct. No preamble, plan, or progress note before or between calls. After result: next call direct or final answer never announce next call. Text before call only to clarify, warn security/irreversible, or resolve ambiguity.
28	
29	Follow explicit reply-language instructions from the user or project. Otherwise preserve the user's dominant language. Never switch because of example text or multilingual context elsewhere. text:
`bot.mjs` is written and passes my 31 checks. Those cover quiet-hour boundaries in summer and winter, India, Japan, bad or missing time zones, opt-out, and odd input such as `null` arguments and a getter that throws. Nothing was sent, and the test script is in `/tmp`, not in your repo.

Checks run in this order, and the first one that matches holds the text:

| `rule` | When it holds the text |
|---|---|
| `invalid-input` | Anything malformed: `now` not a valid Date, unknown `kind`, empty text, missing `sms`, or an unexpected exception. It fails closed and never throws. |
| `opted-out` | `optedOutAt` is anything other than `null` or `undefined`, for any kind of text. An unparseable value still counts as opted out. |
| `no-consent` | Marketing text and `optedIn` is not exactly `true`. |
| `no-valid-time-zone` | Marketing text and the customer's local time can't be worked out. |
| `quiet-hours` | Marketing text outside 8:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. in the customer's own time zone, per 47 CFR 64.1200(c)(1). 9:00:00 p.m. exactly is held. |
| `no-opt-out-notice` | Marketing text with no "STOP" in it. CTIA expects opt-out instructions, and since nothing is stored between calls, every marketing text needs one. |

When the text is allowed, `rule` is the empty string.

Some of these are my judgment calls, so check them:
- **Transactional texts** skip consent, quiet hours and the STOP footer. They are held only if the customer has opted out. A login code goes out even if `optedIn` is false, because the customer gave their number and asked for it. If you'd rather hold those, add a check on `optedIn`.
- **Promotional wording in a transactional text:** a text marked transactional that contains things like "20% off", "use code" or "shop now" is treated as marketing. A shipping notice with a coupon attached counts as a sale text under the FCC rules.
- **Time zone values:** `UTC`, `GMT`, `Etc/*` and bare abbreviations like `EST` are treated as wrong. They are usually a server default, and `EST` ignores daylight saving. A missing or wrong zone holds marketing, because there is no safe hour to guess.
- **Opt-out covers everything:** after a STOP reply, even a login code is held. Use another channel for those customers, such as email.

The function does not check:
- **Sender name:** CTIA wants your business name in the first text, and the function doesn't check for it.
- **Do-not-call lists:** the National Do Not Call Registry is not checked, because there is no input for it.
- **State rules:** some states set stricter hours (for example Florida, 8 p.m. cutoff). India (TRAI) also has its own promotional hours, 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. Only the FCC window is applied.
- **Restricted content:** CTIA's prohibited-content categories (alcohol, tobacco, firearms and similar) are not checked.
